questions.q: What problem does Lakeflow Connect solve beyond what Autoloader already handles?
options: Ingesting from source types that were never "a folder of files" to begin with, like databases, SaaS applications, or message queues
It replaces Autoloader entirely with a completely different file-ingestion mechanism
It only works with Unity Catalog volumes, never DBFS
It has no real difference from Autoloader
questions.explain: Autoloader solves the file-in-a-folder shape specifically; Connect is the broader ingestion layer on top.

questions.q: Does adopting Lakeflow Connect require changing how Autoloader's own code is written?
options: No — nothing about Autoloader's syntax changes; it's understood as one of Connect's ingestion types, specifically the file-based one
Yes, cloudFiles format must be replaced with a new API
Yes, checkpointLocation is no longer needed
Yes, readStream must be replaced entirely
questions.explain: Lakeflow Connect is the umbrella; Autoloader remains the specific tool for the file-arriving-in-a-folder case.

questions.q: What does a managed connector for a SaaS CRM system handle on your behalf?
options: Authentication, schema mapping, and incremental extraction
Only the final aggregation step for gold tables
Row-level security masking
Compute cluster provisioning
questions.explain: This is conceptually the same "managed" idea from Lesson 4 (compute) and Lesson 41 (tables), applied to ingestion.

questions.q: Why does a real organization typically need more than just Autoloader for ingestion?
options: Real organizations' data almost never comes from just one kind of source — Connect's broader connectors make the same medallion pattern usable across many source types
Autoloader is deprecated and no longer functions
Files in a folder are never a valid data source in production
Connect is required even when all data genuinely is files in a folder
questions.explain: NYC Taxi data specifically has always been files in a folder, where Autoloader alone remains the right tool.

questions.q: How does Lakeflow Connect's "managed" concept relate to earlier lessons in this course?
options: It's the same idea Lesson 4 introduced for compute and Lesson 41 introduced for tables, now applied to the ingestion step itself
It's a completely unrelated concept introduced for the first time in this lesson
It only relates to Unity Catalog's access control grants
It relates only to Delta Sharing's recipient concept
questions.explain: Databricks handling the hard part is a recurring pattern across compute, tables, and now ingestion.
